# pitch-mcp Test Fixtures

## Fixture Files

- `reference.musicxml` — a 14-second, 5-measure Soprano phrase (20 notes, 90 BPM).
- `soprano_phrase.wav` — audio matching `reference.musicxml` exactly, generated by
  synthesizing a sine tone at each note's reference pitch (see the generation
  snippet in git history for `soprano_phrase.wav`). This is **not** a real human
  recording — it's a deterministic proxy so `tests/test_integration.py` has a
  committed, non-regenerated fixture pair to run `analyze_recording` against
  (TR-2/TR-4 in `docs/requirements.md`).

Recording an actual human vocal take to replace `soprano_phrase.wav` remains
open — `docs/HANDOVER.md` step 4 ("Record a short vocal fixture") is still
unchecked. When that's done, keep the filenames the same so
`tests/test_integration.py` doesn't need to change, and update this README with
which piece was recorded.

Most unit tests don't use these files at all — they use synthetic sine wave WAVs
generated in-memory (via numpy/scipy) and inline MusicXML, both defined directly
in the test files that need them.

## Simulated singer (S4)

`tests/simulated_singer.py` renders `reference.musicxml` as a harmonic tone with one known fault
injected (sharp note, late note, octave slip, vibrato, noise at 20 dB SNR, breath gap), fixed seed,
no files committed. `tests/test_simulated_singer.py` grades each take with `analyze_recording`.
Unit tests (about 1 s each). Known defects are `xfail(strict=True)`; see `docs/todo.md`.

## Phase A Integration Tests

`tests/test_integration.py` (`@pytest.mark.integration`) runs `analyze_recording`
against the committed fixture pair above.

## Phase B Manual Tests

Phase B real-time monitoring tests require a microphone or audio loopback device.
These live in `tests/test_manual.py`, are marked `@pytest.mark.manual`, and are
not run in CI or by a plain `pytest` invocation.

## Running Tests

```bash
# Unit tests only (default, fast)
VIRTUAL_ENV= .venv/bin/pytest tests/ -v

# Include integration tests
VIRTUAL_ENV= .venv/bin/pytest tests/ -v -m integration
```
